cases.headline: Wausau man pleads not guilty to bail jumping, disorderly conduct charges
cases.summary: Robert Edward Dewayne Stevens Jr., 46, of Wausau, is charged with two misdemeanor counts of bail jumping and one count of disorderly conduct with a domestic abuse modifier, filed March 17. He pleaded not guilty and was released on a $150 cash bond with sobriety and pretrial monitoring conditions.

nextHearing.note: Judicial pretrial, Branch 3, 10:40 a.m., Judge LaMont Jacobson

updates.note: Criminal complaint filed; Stevens pleaded not guilty at his initial appearance and cash bond was set at $150 with sobriety and pretrial monitoring conditions.
Pretrial conference held; judicial pretrial scheduled for Sept. 30.

cases.headline: Wausau man convicted of sexually assaulting child awaits sentencing
cases.summary: Sandro Gerena-Vazquez, 53, of Wausau, was convicted by a Marathon County jury Sept. 24 of first-degree sexual assault of a child and faces up to 60 years in prison. Wausau Pilot & Review does not identify victims of sexual assault.

updates.note: A jury returned a guilty verdict after a three-day trial. Judge Suzanne O’Neill revoked bond and ordered a presentence investigation.

cases.headline: Weston ATM jackpotting suspect set for plea hearing in January
cases.summary: Enhnort Leonardo Araujo Valero, 28, is accused of breaching a Weston credit union ATM in December 2025. He faces two other cases in Marathon County. A single hearing on Jan. 7 and a $25,000 cash bond cover all three.

nextHearing.note: Plea and sentencing hearing, Judge Suzanne O’Neill

updates.note: Judge Suzanne O’Neill set a $25,000 cash bond covering his three Marathon County cases.

cases.headline: Former Kronenwetter trustee faces 43 counts in Schofield dog neglect case
cases.summary: Sean Dumais, 49, a former Kronenwetter village trustee, faces 43 counts, including felony theft in a business setting of more than $100,000 and four felony counts of mistreatment of animals causing death. Investigators say they found starving dogs in October 2025 at Central Wisconsin K-9, his Schofield training business. Two other people are charged in separate cases.

cases.headline: Wausau man charged with killing roommate faces January trial
cases.summary: Dustin Stinson, 35, of Wausau, is charged with first-degree intentional homicide in the Sept. 14, 2025, shooting death of his roommate, Jacob Socha, 31. He pleaded not guilty Jan. 2. A judge lowered his bail from $1 million to $75,000 cash on Oct. 19.

laterHearings.note: Jury trial, expected to last five days

updates.note: Judge Suzanne O’Neill lowered bail from $1 million to $75,000 cash.

cases.headline: Birnamwood man charged with homicide in brother’s stabbing death
cases.summary: Timothy J. Anker, 58, of Birnamwood, is charged with first-degree intentional homicide in the April 26 death of his brother, Thomas J. Anker, 57, at the home they shared in the town of Norrie. He told investigators his brother lunged onto a knife; prosecutors say forensic evidence undermines that account. He remains in custody on a $500,000 cash bond.

updates.note: Charged with first-degree intentional homicide with a domestic abuse modifier.
At his initial appearance, Judge Suzanne O’Neill set bond at $500,000 cash.
Judge Rick Cveykus denied a defense request to reduce the bond.

cases.headline: Weston man charged with attempted homicide in Wausau bar shooting
cases.summary: Jacob Allen Fong Lo, 23, of Weston, is charged with attempted first-degree intentional homicide in an Aug. 2 shooting outside a Wausau bar. A 43-year-old man was struck in the back; police said the wound was not life-threatening. Lo remains in custody on a $250,000 cash bond. A separate case charges him in an Aug. 5 police pursuit.

nextHearing.note: Jury trial, four days, Judge Gregory Strasser

updates.note: Charged with first-degree recklessly endangering safety in the Aug. 2 shooting outside M&R Station.
Prosecutors amended the complaint to attempted first-degree intentional homicide.
After a preliminary hearing, the court found probable cause and bound Lo over for trial.
Judge Gregory Strasser appointed attorney Jay Kronenwetter to represent Lo.
